title: Gas Turbine
model_title: Industrial Gas Turbine (Single Shaft, Can-Annular Combustors)

introduction.definition: A gas turbine compresses air, burns fuel in it and expands the hot gas through a turbine (Brayton cycle). Part of the turbine power drives the compressor; the rest drives a generator or compressor. The hot exhaust can raise steam in a heat-recovery boiler (combined cycle).
key_points: Compressor uses roughly half of turbine work
Efficiency rises with pressure ratio and firing temperature
Inlet air temperature strongly affects output

classification.type: Industrial heavy-duty, single shaft, can-annular combustion

introduction.summary: A gas turbine works on the Brayton cycle: an axial compressor squeezes air, fuel is burned in the combustors at nearly constant pressure, and the hot gas expands through the turbine. The turbine drives the compressor and has power left over for a generator or compressor. The hot exhaust is often used in a heat-recovery boiler (combined cycle).

foundation: Mount on a rigid, level foundation or grouted baseplate sized for the machine mass and dynamic loads (typically ≥3–5 × machine mass for reciprocating machines).
Check for soft foot before final bolting.
alignment: Align driver and driven shafts with a laser or dial-indicator method to the coupling maker's tolerances; re-check hot alignment where thermal growth is significant.
piping: Inlet filtration house, exhaust stack/HRSG, fuel gas conditioning; fire protection in the enclosure.
commissioning: Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Fill lubricant to the correct level and grade.
Start unloaded where possible; record vibration, temperatures, current and pressures as a baseline.

routine.task: Monitor exhaust temperature spread, vibration, compressor ΔP.

lubrication: Forced lube-oil system for bearings; accessory gearbox.

video_tutorials.title: Gas Turbine — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Gas Turbine.
A gas turbine compresses air, burns fuel in it and expands the hot gas through a turbine (Brayton cycle).
Part of the turbine power drives the compressor; the rest drives a generator or compressor.
The hot exhaust can raise steam in a heat-recovery boiler (combined cycle).
Typical applications include power generation (simple and combined cycle); mechanical drive for pipeline compressors; offshore platforms; aircraft and marine propulsion (aero-derivatives).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Compressor, Combustor & Turbine Casings, Air Inlet Bellmouth, Rotor: Compressor & Turbine Blading on a Single Shaft, Exhaust Diffuser & Collector.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Gas Turbine.
Monitor exhaust temperature spread, vibration, compressor ΔP.
Online/offline compressor wash.
Combustion inspection.
Hot-gas-path inspection; major overhaul.
Watch for compressor fouling: lower output, higher heat rate. Common cause: dirty inlet air.
Watch for combustion problems: exhaust temperature spread, flame-out. Common cause: nozzle fouling, liner cracks.
Watch for hot-gas-path damage: borescope findings. Common cause: over-firing, coating loss.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
